title: fix(formula): has() over an indexed or call receiver evaluates as the CEL spec defines it
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-bill"} -->
_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg?thread=cmsg_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg8b7MP77ty5yyBo5R7ks3hC)_

Fixes #25267

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: added

## What was wrong

The CEL spec defines `has(e.f)` for any expression `e`: a presence test on field `f` of whatever `e` evaluates to. cel-js 8.0.0 (the latest release) implements `has()` as a macro whose type-check walks the selection chain back to its root and refuses the argument with `has() invalid argument` unless that root is an identifier. So `has(data.environments[0].storage.usedMb)`, `has(record.items[0].name)` or `has(dyn(x).y)` faulted at every type-check and every evaluation.

Measured on `origin/main` 17f3c65a1d before the change, through `@objectstack/formula`'s public entries:

| door | `has(data.environments[0].storage.usedMb)` | `has(record.a.b)` (control) |
|---|---|---|
| `celEngine.evaluate` | `ok: false`, `has() invalid argument` | `ok: true` |
| `celEngine.compile` | refused | accepted |
| `validateExpression('predicate', …)` (object / flow / action / sharing-rule / hook slots) | refused | accepted |
| `validateVisibilityPredicates` (page and view `visibleWhen`) | **0 findings** | 0 findings |

The page and view gate checks syntax, unknown functions and bare identifiers, never types (the #6253 / #13594 rulings), so on that surface the predicate published clean and then failed open in the console. The fault is cel-js's own (no ObjectStack wrapping is involved), and `Environment.registerFunction('has(ast): bool', …)` cannot replace the built-in macro: cel-js refuses the overlapping signature.

## The fix: the engine evaluates it, as the spec says

The route is the "evaluate" branch of the card. `has()` over an indexed or call receiver is valid CEL, and the engine can honour it without forking cel-js.

`rewriteIndexedHas` (in `cel-engine.ts`, next to the #3306 `rewriteNullableTernary`, built the same way: a parse, an AST walk, a reserialize only when something changed, a bounded memo) lowers such a call to `e.?f.hasValue()`. That is the spec's definition of optional field selection (`e.?f` is `optional.of(e.f)` when `has(e.f)`, else `optional.none()`), so the two are the same test. cel-js evaluates the receiver exactly as its `has()` does: an absent key before the last step still faults `No such key`, and only the last step answers `false`.

- It fires only on a `has()` whose argument is a `.` selection rooted in something other than an identifier. `has(record.a.b)` is left to cel-js. So is every argument the spec itself refuses: a bare name (`has(status)`) and an index as the last step (`has(record.items[0])`) still fault `has() invalid argument` everywhere.
- It is applied at every place cel-js type-checks: `evaluate`, `compile`, `firstUndeclaredReference`, `inferCelType` and the overload-fault probe. The parse-only front end (`parseCelToAst`) keeps the authored `has(…)` call. It already parsed, and AST consumers such as the lint's `has(…)` span mask keep finding the call they key on.
- No lint change is needed. Every rule that judges a CEL predicate reaches the type verdict through `@objectstack/formula` (`validateExpression`, `celEngine.compile`), or does not judge types at all (the page and view rules). They now agree with the runtime.

## Tests

New `packages/formula/src/cel-has-indexed-receiver.test.ts`, 9 tests:

- the filed reading (present answers `true`, absent answers `false`), and agreement with the `'usedMb' in …` form the filing worked around with;
- parity with cel-js's own identifier-rooted `has()` over ten value kinds (map with or without the key, key holding `null` / `false`, empty map, `null`, list, int, string, bool) and two path depths, with faults compared by kind and first line;
- every door gives one verdict: `compile`, `validateExpression`, `evaluate`, `inferCelType` (`bool`), and `firstUndeclaredReference`, which now reports a bare `status` behind an indexed `has()` instead of being masked by the macro's fault;
- controls: `has(status)` and `has(record.items[0])` are still refused by `compile`, `validateExpression` and `evaluate`;
- the rewrite is narrow (five untouched spellings), idempotent, and lowers a `has()` nested inside a lowered receiver.

Ablation at baf8e2254, with an early `return source;` injected into `rewriteIndexedHas` through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: the suite went 8 failed / 1 passed (the controls test is the one that stays green, as it should). The restore was verified as blob == HEAD (`f4f10ad31d5c`) and `git diff HEAD` empty. No `dist/` is involved: the suite imports `./cel-engine` from source.

Runs at head baf8e2254 (under `os-verify-lock.sh`):
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/formula build && … test && … typecheck`: exit 0. Test Files 52 passed (52), Tests 1376 passed (1376).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test`: exit 0. Test Files 153 passed (153), Tests 7076 passed (7076).

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 67 commands at baf8e2254. All 67 were run, with exit codes captured before any pipe, and `--ran` reconciles them: 66 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED, 0 unrun. 66 exited 0. Two of those first exited 3 on missing prerequisites and were 0 on a rerun: `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` after fetching its shallow-clone fixture commit, and `check:lean-entry-closure` after building `@objectstack/objectql`. The NOT-MEASURED one is `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (exit 3, needs every package's `dist`), which is left to CI.

Dogfood: n/a. The title carries no `!` and the `Clause-②` arm is `(widening)`.

## Acceptance notes

- **Why `Clause-②: yes (widening)` / `added`.** The claim expected `no`. Measured from the diff, `validateExpression` used to refuse this argument on object, flow, action, sharing-rule and hook predicates, and now accepts it. That is a wider publish accept set, and a newly accepted value for an author. The changeset is `minor` on `@objectstack/formula` accordingly.
- **A docblock this makes stale, outside the claim's file surface and left alone.** `packages/spec/src/automation/flow-value-slot-template.ts` (`guardOf`) and the test title at `flow-value-slot-template.test.ts:201` say `has()` refuses an index anywhere in its argument at run time. That reason is now false. The behaviour it explains (no guard is printed for a path with a numeric segment) is still right, because a path ending in an index cannot be guarded by `has()`, and an out-of-range index faults instead of answering `false`.
- **The sibling class stays open.** `has(status)` and `has(record.items[0])` on a page or view `visibleWhen` still publish with 0 findings (measured: `validateVisibilityPredicates` against a page component, with `record.x === 1` as the firing control), and still fault at runtime. Closing that means adopting one more `check()` verdict on the page and view rule, which the #13594 ruling ("只拒未知函数裁定,⛔ 不搬运 `check()` 的其他抱怨") reserves for the maintainer. It is not done here.
- **Error excerpts.** A runtime fault inside a lowered call (an absent intermediate key) quotes the lowered source in cel-js's excerpt, the same property the #3306 rewrite already has.
- **Removal.** When cel-js lifts the identifier-root restriction from its `has()` macro, `rewriteIndexedHas` and its five call sites can go, together with its own describe block; the evaluation and every-door pins keep holding.
